doc.title: Sheryl Bailey interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 24, 2023

title: Self-taught guitarists versus trained readers
summary: Rowe and Bailey compare self-taught guitarists, who rely on their ears, with trained musicians, and how each has strengths.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: I’m always fascinated by — guitar players especially who are self-taught, didn’t go to music school. For about six years I played in a group that was playing early Yes and Genesis and very complex music. And the guitar players had an easier time learning it than I did. And I had graduated from music school. And their ability to hear and not get hung up about odd measures or forms was positive for them.

Um hum. Yeah I think, I mean I think there’s finding that balance between I think as guitar players — well that’s always — there’s tons of jokes about sight reading guitarists and stuff that we often learn — it’s the people’s instrument. Someone shows you some chords. Oh here’s the chords to a Beatles song. And you just play it. And there’s an entry point where it’s easy and can sound good easily to a certain degree, and so you can do that for a long time. But you are more oriented towards just your ears, not in an educated way of your ears is where you would study ear training and be able to identify intervals. But you also develop more of an intuitive sense I think you don’t have that fear. I mean I know some amazing — and I know you do too — some amazing classical musicians that are terrified, even if they had to improvise on a session for two bars. But you know I mean I can read and I’m a good reader but I always feel if I have to play, if I had to play a Broadway show or something, I’m like sweating bullets, the pressure of like nailing everything in that kind of precision. So I think wherever you come from you have strengths in different areas. I think the thing, the pursuit about developing our musicianship is to make all those areas as strong as possible so you don’t have weaknesses. But we all have them, you know?
